recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No source follow-up is needed for FHIR-37555; any stale diagram tooltip refresh should happen through the normal diagram generation path, not as a seed issue correction.
issue_request: FHIR-37555 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Subscription change request raised against R4 and applied for R5. It requested a Subscription.managingEntity 0..1 Reference(CareTeam | HealthcareService | Organization | RelatedPerson | Patient | Practitioner | PractitionerRole) to provide authorization context and an entity responsible for Subscription changes without dictating local authorization policy.
initial_application: Commit 7704203868d3f767ed830de3649054899146f5ae, 'late breaking changes including FHIR-37555 and FHIR-32530,' added Subscription.managingEntity to source/subscription/structuredefinition-Subscription.xml with the requested cardinality, target profiles, summary flag, and FiveWs.author mapping. The original definition included the Jira resolution's disclosure-authorization wording.
additional_context: Subscription is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/subscription/structuredefinition-Subscription.xml is in current build scope. Current source keeps Subscription.managingEntity and includes the original target profiles plus Device and Group from later FHIR-47337. The current definition and comment differ from the seed resolution because later Applied/Persuasive issue FHIR-47340 intentionally replaced the disclosure-oriented definition with communication-with-server wording and a server-managed Subscriptions note. FHIR-47340 and FHIR-47337 already have Issue-Reconcile-Key audit commits on the combined branch. A checked-in subscription.svg tooltip still contains the old definition, but it is a generated-looking diagram artifact and not a reason to change authoritative source for FHIR-37555.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current authoritative source already preserves the Subscription.managingEntity element requested by FHIR-37555, and restoring the original disclosure wording would conflict with the later FHIR-47340 clarification.
